findings.source_passage: Some men die at ebb tide; some at low water; some at the full of the flood;—and I feel now like a billow that's all one crested comb, Starbuck.
findings.source_locator: farewell dialogue between Ahab and Starbuck, just before 'I am old;—shake hands with me, man'
findings.why_it_matters: This rhythmically distinctive line encodes Ahab's self-awareness of his imminent death through the tidal motif and is a critically noted passage; its loss flattens the farewell to bare sentiment.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the 'ebb tide / low water / full of the flood' sentence verbatim before 'I am old;—shake hands with me, man' in the farewell exchange.

findings.source_passage: Aye, he's chasing _me_ now; not I, _him_—that's bad; I might have known it, too. Fool! the lines—the harpoons he's towing.
findings.source_locator: after 'Nothing! and noon at hand! The doubloon goes a-begging!'
findings.why_it_matters: The italicized reversal—'he's chasing me now; not I, him'—is an interpretive keystone: Ahab explicitly recognizes the inversion of predator and prey, a moment critics return to repeatedly. The draft's paraphrase ('I've oversailed him—got the start!') erases the reversal entirely.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore Ahab's italicized reversal verbatim: 'he's chasing _me_ now; not I, _him_—that's bad' after the 'Nothing! and noon at hand!' line.

findings.source_passage: he tears the vane"—pointing to the red flag flying at the main-truck—"Ha! he soars away with it!—Where's the old man now? see'st thou that sight, oh Ahab!—shudder, shudder!"
findings.source_locator: end of Starbuck's visionary monologue, after 'Crazed;—aloft there!—keep thy keenest eye upon the boats'
findings.why_it_matters: The hawk tearing the vane and 'shudder, shudder' is the climax of Starbuck's prophetic vision, anticipating the sky-hawk in the final sinking scene; its absence severs the internal echo that gives the closing image its full weight.
findings.suggested_fix: Append the hawk-tears-the-vane conclusion to Starbuck's monologue, ending with 'shudder, shudder!' before transitioning to the sounding scene.

findings.source_passage: frozen calm, this old skull cracks so, like a glass in which the contents turned to ice, and shiver it. And still this hair is growing now
findings.source_locator: middle of Ahab's long opening monologue, between the 'coolness and a calmness' sentence and the Greenland ice/Vesuvius lava passage
findings.why_it_matters: The frozen-skull image and growing-hair meditation are distinctively Melvillean voice material that establish the monologue's oscillation between cold fatalism and organic life; their elision (marked only with '...') flattens the monologue's rhetorical arc.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore at minimum the 'frozen calm, this old skull cracks so, like a glass' image and the Greenland ice/Vesuvius lava comparison before the wind passage.

summary: Three medium-severity losses—the 'ebb tide / full of the flood' death-harbinger line, Ahab's italicized 'he's chasing me now; not I, him' reversal, and the hawk-tears-the-vane climax of Starbuck's vision—together trigger regeneration; collectively they erase key interpretive moments the critical tradition depends on.
